title: If you're coming
goal: Set a condition about what is already so, with bolsa after a participle or a noun.

intro.text: For a condition about what is already so, planned or done, use a participle or a noun and add *bolsa* with the person: *gelýän bolsaň* (if you're coming), *gitjek bolsaň* (if you're going to go), *okan bolsaň* (if you've read it), *ýadaw bolsaň* (if you're tired).

vocab.en: as for, while (right after a subject: mende bolsa, as for me)

exercises.question: How do you say **if you're coming** (if that's the plan)?

why.1: *Bolsa* with no ending is **if he** or **she**. For **you**: *bolsaň*.
why.2: `-sA` doesn't go on a participle. Keep *gelýän* and add *bolsaň*.

exercises.explain: *gelýän* (coming) + *bolsaň* (if you are): the person goes on *bolsa*.

exercises.label: *gelýän bolsa*: if I'm coming, if you're coming…

accept: gelýän bolsam
gelýän bolsaň
gelýän bolsa
gelýän bolsak
gelýän bolsaňyz
gelýän bolsalar
gelýän bolsa

exercises.explain: *Gelýän* never changes; *bolsa* takes the past endings: *-m, -ň*, nothing, *-k, -ňyz, -lar*.

exercises.en: If you've read the book, give it to me.

accept: ň

exercises.explain: *okan* (read, done) + *bolsaň* (if you are): if you've read it.

exercises.prompt: If you're going to Mary, bring me a melon.
accept: Mara gidýän bolsaň, maňa bir gawun getir.
Eger (sen) Mara [gidýän|gitjek] bolsaň, maňa (bir) gawun getir.
(Sen) Mara gitjek bolsaň, maňa (bir) gawun getir.
Sen Mara gidýän bolsaň, maňa (bir) gawun getir.
Mara gidýän bolsaň, maňa gawun getir.
(Eger) (siz) Mara [gidýän|gitjek] bolsaňyz, maňa (bir) gawun [getiriň|getiriňiz].
(Eger) (sen) Mara gitseň, maňa (bir) gawun getir.
(Eger) (siz) Mara gitseňiz, maňa (bir) gawun [getiriň|getiriňiz].

reject.answer: Mara gidýän bolsa, maňa bir gawun getir.
reject.why: *Bolsa* is **if he** or **she** is going. For **you**: *gidýän bolsaň*.

exercises.explain: *Mara* (to Mary) + *gidýän bolsaň* (if you're going). *Gitjek bolsaň* (if you're going to go) works too.

accept: If you are hungry, eat something.
If you are hungry, [eat|have something to eat|have a meal|have some food].
[Eat|Eat something|Have something to eat] if you are hungry.

exercises.question: Which sentence checks a plan you may already have: **if you're coming tomorrow, call**?
exercises.explain: *Gelýän bolsaň*: if you're coming (if that's the plan). *Ertir gelseň* would be **if you come tomorrow**, a mere possibility.
*bol-* + *-sa* + *-ňyz* (you, plural or polite): back vowels throughout.

exercises.prompt: If you're tired, have a rest.

reject.why: *Bolsa* with no ending is **if he** or **she** is tired. For **you**: *bolsaň*.
`-sA` doesn't go on an adjective. Add *bolsaň*: *ýadaw bolsaň*.

exercises.explain: An adjective with *bolsa* and the person: *ýadaw bolsaň*, if you're tired.

exercises.question: *Men öýde galaryn, Aýna bolsa işe gider.* What does *bolsa* mean here?

why.1: No participle or predicate comes before it, only the subject *Aýna*, and the sentence goes on to its own verb.

exercises.explain: Right after a subject, *bolsa* contrasts two people: I'll stay at home, while Aýna will go to work.

According to the (weather) forecast, tomorrow [it|the weather] will be dry.
The (weather) forecast says [it|the weather] will be dry tomorrow.

exercises.en: If you don't have time, come tomorrow.

accept: sa

reject.why: The **you** is already in *wagtyňyz* (your time). *Bolsa* stays in the third person: *wagtyňyz ýok bolsa*.

exercises.explain: *Wagtyňyz ýok* (you have no time) + *bolsa*: the possessive says whose time.
